scenicChapters.title: Ethiopia Simien Mountains Road
scenicChapters.narrative: Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast. For 47 km this is Ethiopia Simien Mountains Road, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it.

title: Ethiopia Bale Mountains Road
slogan: Shashamane to Harenna Forest · 178 km home again

waypoints.name: Sanetti Plateau
waypoints.advice: Sanetti Plateau, late in the day at 4000 m. The road climbs 4000 m over the 91 km before it, steadily. Reckon on about 26 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Nothing on this route is higher. Next is Harenna Forest, 90 km on and mostly downhill.

waypoints.advice: Back at Harenna Forest. That is the ride.

sections.advice: Shashamane → Dodola is 87 km of getting across. Ride it tidily and keep the enthusiasm for what comes after.
Dodola → Dinsho is 85 km of getting across. Ride it tidily and keep the enthusiasm for what comes after.
Dinsho → Sanetti Plateau climbs about 4000 m in 32 km. This is the part worth slowing down for - look through the bends and use the pull-offs.
Sanetti Plateau → Harenna Forest drops about 4000 m over 25 km. Brakes and eyes forward; the views are behind the corners, not in them.

scenicChapters.title: Ethiopia Bale Mountains Road
scenicChapters.narrative: The valley floor is behind you and the road starts working for its height at about 12.5%. Corners stack above one another where the ground allows nothing straighter — first and second gear more often than not. Look through each corner to the next one and let the engine do the holding.

scenicChapters.title: Ethiopia Bale Mountains Road
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 4000 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance. Cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.
